primary_topics: Keynote address at the NUSP 36th National Student Congress on NUS's 50th anniversary, December 15, 2007

CJP's personal founding narrative: the September 1957 walk-out from SCAP and CONDA; the rejection of a lucrative international vice-presidency offered by SCAP to placate him; the formation of NUSP with student leaders from UP, UST, San Beda and other schools

The NUSP founding vision and core values: unite student opinion, free youth from political interference, fight communist infiltration, redirect youth to constructive idealism; core values -- dignity, integrity, independence, liberty, responsibility, democracy

Challenge to current students: tackle the present plagues (poverty, malgovernance, corruption, EJKs), have their own vision and values in writing, and be able to show them to their children 50 years hence
sub_topics: CJP's extraordinary statement: 'I have lived on this planet for over seventy years; have met some of the most important people that populate it during my lifetime; have traveled to all the continents of our earth, except Antarctica. Yet let me tell you very candidly that I would exchange all of that to turn back the hands of time and to relive my years as a student leader.'

Three-fold NUSP theme: (1) look back -- connect with the legacy; (2) improve the future -- advance rights and welfare; (3) foster the present -- strengthen NUSP; 'every person and every organization must have a vision of what he, she or it intends to accomplish, a method of fulfilling them, and a set of immutable values to guide the journey'

Cold War context: world divided between liberal democracies (US) and totalitarian-communist states (USSR); communists infiltrated Filipino student organizations; government tried to corral them in the Consultative Council of Students

The 1957 walk-out: CJP as new FEU CSO president questioned SCAP and CONDA's communist and partisan activities; SCAP leaders tried to placate him by unanimously electing him as VP for International Affairs (free travel to many countries, pocket money from Malacañang); 'notwithstanding all these, I chose the more difficult, straight and narrow path by seceding from both the SCAP and the CONDA, rejecting my lucrative position in SCAP, and refusing membership in the President's august Little Cabinet'
NUSP founding partners: student leaders from UP, UST, San Beda College, St. Theresa's, National University and Sta. Isabel joined the walk-out and formed the NUSP nucleus

NUSP founding vision: 'pledged to unite and reflect faithfully student opinion on current national issues, free the youth from undue political interferences, fight communist infiltration in the campuses, and redirect the youth's thinking and energy to constructive idealism'
NUSP founding core values: dignity, integrity, independence, liberty, responsibility and democracy
NUSP achievements: 'the communist effort to infiltrate student movements failed; freedom prevailed; and the students were liberated from the political and partisan apron strings of the government'

Challenge to students: 'I expect you to tackle these plagues, denounce their perpetrators, and offer some perspectives and solutions. Do you each have a vision and values to guide you in the next fifty years of your life? Please put them in writing and include them in your digital files, so that fifty years from now, in the presence of your children and grandchildren, you may show these mementos.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered December 15, 2007 as the keynote at the NUSP 36th National Student Congress -- the 50th anniversary of the NUSP's founding -- this address by CJP opens with the most candid personal preference statement in the corpus: 'I have lived on this planet for over seventy years; have met some of the most important people that populate it; have traveled to all the continents of our earth, except Antarctica. Yet let me tell you very candidly that I would exchange all of that to turn back the hands of time and to relive my years as a student leader.' He narrates the NUSP founding: in September 1957, as the newly elected FEU CSO president, CJP questioned the communist and partisan activities in SCAP and CONDA; SCAP tried to placate him by unanimously electing him VP for International Affairs (free travel, Malacañang pocket money); 'notwithstanding all these, I chose the more difficult, straight and narrow path by seceding from both the SCAP and CONDA, rejecting my lucrative position in SCAP, and refusing membership in the President's august Little Cabinet.' Student leaders from UP, UST, San Beda, St. Theresa's, National University and Sta. Isabel joined the walk-out, forming the NUSP nucleus. The founding vision: 'pledged to unite and reflect faithfully student opinion on current national issues, free the youth from undue political interferences, fight communist infiltration in the campuses, and redirect the youth's thinking and energy to constructive idealism.' Core values: dignity, integrity, independence, liberty, responsibility, democracy. Achievements: 'the communist effort to infiltrate student movements failed; freedom prevailed; and the students were liberated from the political and partisan apron strings of the government.' For today's students: tackle the present plagues (poverty, malgovernance, corruption, EJKs); have a vision and values; 'put them in writing and include them in your digital files, so that fifty years from now, in the presence of your children and grandchildren, you may show these mementos and declare before God and man that you have lived your life in accordance with these cherished ideals.'
